competitive_position.basis: Stated as management belief in the 10-Q MD&A.
competitive_position.claim: Management positions BRIUMVI within the anti-CD20 class mainly on convenience: a one-hour infusion given twice a year after the starting dose.
quotes: BRIUMVI is administered as a one-hour, twice per year infusion following the starting dose.

We believe BRIUMVI’s clinical profile, including its one-hour infusion time and twice-annual dosing schedule, together with demonstrated efficacy and safety in pivotal trials and accumulating real-world experience, supports its positioning within the anti-CD20 therapeutic class.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 8-K release and the 10-Q MD&A.
competitive_position.claim: Seven-year follow-up of the ULTIMATE I & II trials showed an annualized relapse rate of 0.018 in year seven, with 88.3% of continuously treated patients free from 24-week confirmed disability progression.
quotes: BRIUMVI demonstrated sustained efficacy with an annualized relapse rate (ARR) of 0.018 in the seventh year of treatment and 88.3% of continuously treated patients remaining free from 24-week confirmed disability progression.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 8-K release; the share-taking mechanism is inferred from the switcher proportion.
competitive_position.claim: The Phase 4 ENABLE real-world study covered 1,076 participants, 30% of whom switched from prior CD20 therapy, and 99.2% remained relapse-free on BRIUMVI.
quotes: Updated data from 1,076 participants, 30% of whom switched from prior CD20 therapy, showed that 99.2% remained relapse-free during BRIUMVI treatment, with an ARR of 0.014.

competitive_position.claim: In October 2026 a five-year matching-adjusted indirect comparison of BRIUMVI against ocrelizumab and ofatumumab was published. Those two drugs are anti-CD20 competitors named in the evidence.
quotes: In October 2026, results from a five-year matching-adjusted indirect comparison (MAIC) evaluating long-term relapse activity and disability progression outcomes with BRIUMVI® (ublituximab-xiiy) compared with ocrelizumab and ofatumumab in patients with relapsing multiple sclerosis (RMS) were published online in Multiple Sclerosis and Related Disorders.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A and the 8-K release.
competitive_position.claim: The Phase 3 ENHANCE trial met its primary endpoint for a single 600 mg starting infusion that removes the Day 15 infusion. A potential launch of this simplified IV initiation is cited for mid-2027.
quotes: The trial met its primary endpoint, demonstrating bioequivalent drug exposure between the currently approved BRIUMVI initiation infusion dosing regimen of 150 mg on Day 1 and 450 mg on Day 15 and a consolidated single 600 mg infusion on Day 1, eliminating the need for a Day 15 infusion.
a potential launch of simplified IV initiation in mid-2027

competitive_position.claim: Threat: the company describes the RMS market as highly competitive, with numerous approved disease-modifying therapies.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A and the 10-K risk factors.
competitive_position.claim: Threat: new branded products or biosimilars, pricing and contracting strategies, and payer utilization management may shape competitive dynamics.

The key competitive factors affecting the success of all of our drug candidates, if approved, are likely to be their efficacy, safety, convenience, price, the level of generic or biosimilar competition and the availability of reimbursement from government and other third-party payors.

competitive_position.claim: Threat: uptake depends on factors such as established prescribing practices, patient switching dynamics and competitive contracting.

competitive_position.claim: Threat: many competitors have significantly greater financial, development, manufacturing and commercialization resources.
